title: What the Narrow Waist of the Internet Means for Innovation Today

reader_summary.headline: Today's episode is one of our intimate hallway-style conversations, or as intimate as remote work allows anyway.
reader_summary.overview: Today's episode is one of our intimate hallway-style conversations, or as intimate as remote work allows anyway. It's all about the history and future of protocol development. A16Z crypto partner Ali Yahya, formerly machine research at Google Brain, wrote a tweet storm earlier this year about the narrow waste of blockchain computing.

key_points.text: Ali observed that the internet protocol, which emerged at a research labs and government funding decades ago.
key_points.evidence_quote: Ali observed that the internet protocol, which emerged at a research labs and government funding decades ago, has has taken the world from zero devices to more than 15 billion connected devices today.

key_points.text: What was it about the internet protocol that allowed building so many applications on top?
key_points.evidence_quote: What was it about the internet protocol that allowed building so many applications on top?

key_points.text: Helping us answer this question is A16Z general partner in enterprise, Martin Casato, who pioneered software-defined networking.
key_points.evidence_quote: Helping us answer this question is A16Z general partner in enterprise, Martin Casato, who pioneered software-defined networking.

key_points.text: He co-founded Nassira, which was acquired by VMware, and then he led their networking and security business unit.
key_points.evidence_quote: He co-founded Nassira, which was acquired by VMware, and then he led their networking and security business unit, which he scaled to a hugely successful business, so he knows a thing or two about this topic.

thesis: The discussion argues that the internet's success stemmed from TCP/IP acting as a minimalist, unopinionated aggregator that enabled a powerful economic flywheel between bandwidth providers and application developers. The speakers further contend that similar narrow waist phenomena can emerge through either concerted community efforts or technology monopolies, both of which solve the cold-start problem of two-sided markets like the internet, Lyft, and Airbnb.
